summary: This House resolution supports designating May 10-16 2026 as Taiwanese American Heritage Week and celebrates the contributions of Taiwanese Americans to the United States.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is purely symbolic and contains no provisions, authorizations, or references related to federal spending levels or appropriations. It neither expands nor reduces government spending.
No language in the bill addresses tax policy, rates, credits, or revenue measures of any kind.
The bill makes no reference to healthcare systems, coverage models, or medical policy.
No provisions or mentions related to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues appear in the text.
While the resolution honors existing Taiwanese Americans, it proposes no changes to immigration law, visas, pathways, or enforcement.
The bill contains zero references to reproductive rights or abortion policy.
Mentions of Taiwanese Americans serving in the Armed Forces are purely descriptive and do not alter defense spending or military policy.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate-related content is present.
The resolution does not engage with welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety-net policy.
References to educators and scholars are honorific only and do not affect education funding, policy, or structure.
No mention of drugs, enforcement, or decriminalization appears.
The bill does not address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The resolution notes Taiwan's role as an economic partner and semiconductor collaborator but does not enact, modify, or direct any trade policy, tariffs, or agreements.
No fiscal, deficit, or debt-related provisions are included.
The bill contains no language concerning LGBTQ+ protections or rights.
While referencing the Taiwan Relations Act and bilateral partnership, the resolution does not authorize, expand, or reduce foreign aid.
No provisions related to voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures are present.
Mentions of semiconductor leadership are descriptive and do not regulate technology companies or privacy standards.
The bill does not address labor rights, unions, or workplace regulations.
No content relating to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law appears.
